facts.statement: Researchers compared swallowing test results from times when patients were on their medication versus times when they were not.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The timing of the test relative to medication significantly changed the scores for bedside screens, video swallow studies, and dietary advice.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Bedside swallowing screen scores were better when tests happened during the medication's effective window.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Doctors more often suggested changing liquid food textures when the video swallow study was done outside the medication window.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The authors note that because the study design was observational, they cannot prove that the medication itself causes the changes in swallowing.
facts.subject: humans
